Apply for IFAP ↗

Program Structure

  • Duration: 16 Weeks
  • Total Contact Hours: 100 Hours
  • Location: TRACE Expert City
  • Time: Saturdays, 9am to 4pm

Format:

  • Workshops
  • Development Labs
  • Structured Mentorship
  • Industry Simulations
  • Live Pitch Forum

Who This Is For

  • Film industry professionals
  • Emerging and aspiring filmmakers
  • Writers, directors, and producers seeking international pathways
  • Creators developing feature films or high-end series

Core Pillars

1. Development and Dramaturgy

Advanced structural refinement, character architecture, thematic cohesion, and tonal calibration. Emphasis is placed on cross cultural accessibility while preserving authorial identity.

2. Screenwriting for the International Market

Crafting scripts that are structurally rigorous, emotionally legible, genre aware, and internationally readable.

3. Directorial Voice and Genre Strategy

Exploration of genre mechanics, cinematic grammar, and tonal authorship. Each filmmaker develops a cohesive directorial strategy aligned with target markets.

4. Visual Translation and Storyboarding

Translating narrative intention into visual architecture through shot design, mood frameworks, aesthetic references, and cinematic continuity planning.

5. International Film Business and Finance

Global financing structures, co production treaties, packaging strategies, talent attachment models, and navigating key film markets.

6. Sales, Distribution and Festival Strategy

Territory sales, streaming acquisitions, presales models, and long term rights strategy. Participants learn how projects are evaluated commercially across territories.

7. Pitch and Market Readiness

Development of industry standard pitch decks, verbal pitching frameworks, and investor facing materials.

8. Film Aesthetics and Cinematic Identity

Cinematic philosophy, authorship, and positioning to ensure each filmmaker’s creative voice aligns with international audience expectations.

Program Leads & Mentors

Application Requirements

1. Curriculum Vitae (CV)

A detailed professional resume highlighting your experience in film or related creative fields.

2. Cover Letter

A personal statement explaining:

  • Motivation for the program
  • Why you are a strong fit
  • What you aim to achieve
  • Long-term professional ambitions

3. Project Submission (optional)

A project you intend to develop during the program:

  • Logline: Concise summary
  • Synopsis: 1-2 pages (Structure, Character, Theme)

Feature films and high-end series concepts only.

Project Submission Disclaimer

Submission of a project as part of the application process is entirely optional and is requested only to assist the program leaders and selection committee in evaluating applicants. While applicants may choose to apply without submitting a project, providing one can help the committee better understand the applicant’s creative vision and development goals.

All materials submitted will be reviewed solely for the purpose of the selection process. Access will be limited to the Program Director and the designated Selection Committee responsible for evaluating applications.

Any project material submitted will remain the full intellectual property of the applicant. The program, its organizers, and its representatives will not reproduce, distribute, or share the submitted material outside the evaluation process. Submission of a project does not transfer, license, or assign any rights to the program or its organizers.

By submitting a project, applicants acknowledge that the material is being shared voluntarily for evaluation purposes only.

Program Investment

LKR 150,000
Program Fee

+ LKR 2,000 Registration Fee

Installment plans available.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is T2T a university program?

No. T2T is not a degree-awarding university program. It is an industry-readiness and skill-bridging program designed to support students and graduates.

Will I get a job after T2T?

T2T does not guarantee employment. However, it is designed to improve your employability by helping you build skills, confidence, exposure, and portfolio evidence.

Is this only for IT students?

CRISP Batch 4 is mainly suitable for IT, computing, software engineering, and related students. Students from related fields who want digital and industry-readiness skills may also apply.

Do I need to be technically strong?

You do not need to be an expert. But you should have a basic learning foundation and a willingness to improve.

What is the difference between Foundation and Practitioner?

Foundation is a 2-month career-readiness and industry-readiness program. Practitioner is a 6-month pathway that includes Foundation plus 4 months of mentor-driven industry project exposure.

Why is there a fee?

The fee supports program coordination, mentor involvement, workshops, learning activities, operations, assessment, and the guided experience provided to participants.

Is there a certificate?

Participants who complete the required activities may receive certification or recognition based on their completion level.

How do I apply?

Click the Apply for Batch 4 button or contact the T2T team via WhatsApp.

What is T2T AI-X?

This is not an academic course or a generic prompting camp. It is a high-performance career acceleration cohort designed for the AI-assisted software engineering era.

Phase 1

4-Weeks Intensive AI-Native Acceleration

A high-density operational phase covering the mechanics of AI-assisted engineering:

  • Interactive live workshops & technical coaching
  • Hands-on AI-assisted SDLC workflows
  • Systems thinking & architecture engineering
  • Building structural AI-augmented systems
  • Personal capability tracking & portfolio creation
Phase 2

Guided Industry-Aligned Execution

Selected cohort members transition into practical execution spaces:

  • Collaboration on live sandbox projects
  • Exposure to realistic engineering backlogs
  • Code reviews and structural audit sessions
  • Guided production releases & systems optimization
  • Advanced portfolio hardening for global readiness

Who is AI-X built for?

We filter candidates heavily. This acceleration space is designed exclusively for Sri Lankan technical talent aiming to achieve global competitive competency.

IT/Software Engineering graduates and final-year students who realize classroom concepts lag behind modern team operations.

Early-Career Engineers

⚠️ Important: T2T AI-X requires absolute commitment, discipline, and daily consistency. Prepare for a high-intensity acceleration culture.

Frequently Asked Questions

Everything you need to know about the AI-X acceleration structure.

Is this a beginner program?

No. T2T AI-X requires basic programming competency. You should understand syntax, logic loops, basic data structures, and database calls before applying.

Is this online or physical?

This is a hybrid accelerator. It includes virtual mentoring sessions, online backlog operations, and core physical workshop sessions at the TRACE premises in Colombo.

What is the weekly commitment?

Participants must commit at least 40 hours per week for code building, prompts creation, peer reviews, and mentorship standups. It is designed to mirror a full-time software engineering role.

Will this help me become industry ready?

Yes, AI-X is built to replace the standard academic-style project path with actual software backlog cycles. You will work with production-grade AI tools, architecture systems, and code review criteria.

Is this academic or practical?

Entirely practical. We skip textbook definitions to focus on real system execution, prompt pipeline design, software architecture structure, and collaborative repository operations.

Who should apply?

Final year IT/software engineering undergraduates, fresh graduates, junior developers, and self-taught coders who want to build global-ready operational engineering capacity fast.

Do I need prior AI experience?

No prior AI experience is required. We will teach you prompt engineering, copilot patterns, multi-agent frameworks, and database retrieval models from the ground up, assuming you have coding logic down.

What happens after the first 3 months?

Upon successfully completing the Phase 1 assessment gate, you will transition to Phase 2, where you will build advanced projects and collaborate on active sandboxes aligned with industry sponsors.

Frequently Asked Questions

Get answers to common queries regarding the Lead-x program structure and expectations.

Is this only for management students?

No. The program is suitable for students and graduates from business, management, IT, computer science, finance, HR, marketing, engineering, logistics, hospitality, and other general backgrounds. Any student who wants to transition successfully to corporate leadership is encouraged to apply.

Do I need prior AI or data knowledge?

No. The program starts with practical foundations. We do not teach coding or machine learning algorithms; instead, we focus on how managers use data dashboards and AI tools in real business situations to speed up operations and draft quality deliverables.

Is this a traditional lecture-based course?

No. Traditional courses focus on passive learning. T2T Lead-x runs on an active studio model: interactive workshops, weekly practical assignments, mentorship critiques, and a final Boardroom Challenge simulating an executive board proposal.

Will this guarantee a management trainee job?

No program can guarantee a job. However, T2T Lead-x is designed to significantly improve your readiness, confidence, and employability for management trainee and executive-track roles. You will exit the program with a portfolio and corporate presentation experience that sets you far ahead of general applicants.

What is the fee?

The fee is LKR 10,000 per month for 3 months, totaling LKR 30,000 for the initial core training. The full Lead-x journey extends through 20 weeks with an 8-week real business challenge, and top performers may be offered a paid internship after the first 3 months.

Who should apply?

Final-year undergraduates, fresh graduates, early-career professionals (0-2 years of experience), and anyone preparing for management trainee or future leadership selection processes.

T2T FOR ORGANIZATIONS

Build the capability.
Move your business.

From digital foundations to organizational transformation. Align your people, leadership, and ways of working around the challenges that matter to you.

Start a conversation ↗
Digital readinessApplied AILeadershipLasting change

ONE CONTINUOUS JOURNEY

A clear path.
At every stage.

Start where your organization is today. Explore the five stages of the T2T capability journey.

01FoundationWorkforce Baseline

Building baseline digital fluency across the workforce — establishing the essential literacy, tools, and mindset shifts required before advanced capabilities can stick.

Focus areas
Digital literacy, AI tool adoption, security awareness, and workflow mindset shifts.
Expected deliverable
Workforce-wide baseline readiness certification & standardized toolchain onboarding.
Who it supports
All operational, administrative, and frontline technical team members.
02CapabilityRole-Specific Skills

Role- and function-specific skill development, including AI-augmented workflows, ensuring teams apply what they learn directly to day-to-day operations.

Focus areas
AI coding assistants, automated code reviews, prompt engineering, & function-specific AI tooling.
Expected deliverable
Applied project portfolios, measurable velocity gains, & internal workflow automation.
Who it supports
Software engineers, product managers, data analysts, & technical leads.
03LeadershipExecutive Alignment

Equipping decision-makers with the strategic clarity needed to guide change — connecting capability to prioritization, governance, and organizational judgment.

Focus areas
AI governance, resource prioritization, ROI tracking, & change management leadership.
Expected deliverable
Organizational AI roadmap, risk mitigation matrix, & executive steering framework.
Who it supports
VPs of Engineering, CTOs, Engineering Directors, & Executive Leadership.
04TransformationStructural Integration

Embedding new ways of working into core structures and culture — transitioning from isolated individual skills to systematic organizational change.

Focus areas
CI/CD & AI pipeline integration, team restructuring, & agile culture evolution.
Expected deliverable
Redefined engineering processes, updated performance metrics, & enterprise knowledge base.
Who it supports
Entire technical organization & cross-functional business units.
05Sustained GrowthAutonomous Innovation

The organization evolves autonomously. Innovation becomes an ingrained operational habit rather than an external initiative we need to drive for you.

Focus areas
Continuous learning loops, internal R&D spikes, & self-sustaining tech communities.
Expected deliverable
Internal innovation guild, continuous capability benchmarking, & self-evolving tech stack.
Who it supports
Self-driven enterprise innovation teams & organizational leaders.
PRECISION CALIBRATION

How We Diagnose

Before we design anything, we assess. A short diagnostic places your organization on the maturity curve — so what we build next is calibrated to where you actually are, not where you assume you are.

Workforce Digital Literacy

Evaluating baseline digital tool fluency and AI adoption across frontline teams.

Leadership Change Readiness

Assessing executive readiness to govern, prioritize, and support capability shifts.

Process Friction Analysis

Identifying structural bottlenecks and legacy workflow habits holding back velocity.

Stage Placement & Roadmap

Delivering an objective stage placement with an actionable recommended starting stage.

EXECUTION METHODOLOGY

How We Deliver

One consistent method runs through every stage of the journey — only the content, scope, and depth change based on your placement.

1. Applied Workshops

Interactive, facilitator-led intensive sessions focused on immediate practical application rather than passive slides.

2. Structured Self-Work

Take-home application tasks designed directly around your company's live business challenges between sessions.

3. Direct Coaching

One-on-one and team coaching sessions that translate classroom concepts into effective daily practice.

4. Embedded Follow-Through

Structured check-ins at 30, 60, and 90 days to ensure momentum continues after formal engagement concludes.

MULTIDISCIPLINARY NETWORK

The People Behind It

Delivered by a curated network of senior consultants, academic practitioners, and domain experts — tailored per engagement.

Industry Consultants

Seasoned technology leaders bringing real-world delivery and digital transformation experience from global tech firms.

Academic Practitioners

University-affiliated researchers bringing battle-tested pedagogical frameworks and rigorous methodological foundation.

Subject-Matter Specialists

Niche domain experts brought into specific phases based on your organization's exact sector and technology requirements.

CLARITY & GOVERNANCE

Frequently Asked Questions

Everything leadership teams ask before engaging with T2T Corporate Programs.

How does T2T Corporate differ from sending employees to open courses?

Open courses treat individuals in isolation. T2T Corporate Programs evaluate your entire organization's maturity curve, aligning frontline teams, middle management, and executive leaders around your actual internal projects and tech stack.

How is the initial Diagnostic Assessment conducted?

Our diagnostic involves a lightweight combination of digital surveys, team capability sampling, and short stakeholder interviews. It takes minimal team bandwidth while providing a clear baseline of your current maturity stage.

Can the content be customized to our internal tools and proprietary workflows?

Yes. All workshops, self-work, and coaching are customized to incorporate your organization's specific toolchains, security guidelines, coding standards, and internal product goals.

How do you handle IP, security, and data privacy during engagements?

We operate under strict enterprise NDAs and privacy frameworks. Hands-on exercises utilize your sandbox environments or local privacy-compliant AI setups so your proprietary code and data never leave your control.

THEORY TO TRADE BY TRACE

Research Excellence Workshop

Past event · 7 March 2026This workshop has concluded. Explore the details below or contact T2T for future workshops.

Dos & Don’ts every research student and early-stage researcher must know

A practical, experience-driven workshop designed to help research students and early-stage researchers avoid some common pitfalls and complete research with clarity and confidence.

Ask about future workshops

Why this workshop?

Every year, many students start research projects with enthusiasm but struggle due to unclear topics, weak research gaps, unrealistic plans, or loss of motivation. These challenges are common and preventable. This workshop addresses the real, often unspoken issues that derail research early on and provides practical guidance to help you define a clear direction, plan realistically, and stay motivated so you can progress confidently and complete your research successfully.

Common challenges we see:

  • Identifying research gaps and formulating a research-worthy problem/issue and questions
  • Devising a realistic research plan
  • Losing the initial enthusiasm
  • Building a positive relationship with research supervisor/s and other stakeholders

What Makes This Workshop Different

This is not a traditional “research methodology” session.

  • This face-to-face interactive session aims to ensure that participants leave with a tentative research problem and a realistic plan
  • Builds on real experiences of the facilitators as academics/researchers, supervisors and examiners
  • Focuses on decisions, trade-offs, and mistakes
  • Provides practical guidance
  • Relevant for both full-time/part time students and working professionals

About the Facilitators

Prof. Arosha Adikaram and Prof. Tharusha Gooneratne

Chair Professors at the Faculty of Management and Finance,
University of Colombo

With extensive experience in supervising, mentoring, and examining postgraduate researchers over decades, and with deep insight into research progression, completion and publishing. They have also won numerous awards nationally and internationally for research excellence.

Together, they are the authors of 200 Do’s & Don’ts For Management Research Students, a practical guide based on repeated patterns observed among real research students.

Who should attend

This workshop is ideal for management research students/researchers, specifically:

  • Doctoral students (PhD, DBA)
  • MBA, MSc, or MPhil students
  • Final-year undergraduates research students
  • Working professionals planning postgraduate research
  • Researchers who are struggling to progress or complete on time

What the Workshop Covers

This workshop will guide participants through the essential foundations and practical realities of completing high-quality management research, including:

  • Identifying research gaps and formulating a research-worthy problem and questions in business/management research
  • Devising a realistic research plan and executing a high-quality study
  • Maintaining initial enthusiasm and sustaining research momentum
  • Building a constructive and positive relationship with research supervisors and key stakeholders

Key Details

  • Date: 7th March, 2026
  • Time: 9.30AM to 4.30PM
  • Venue: TRACE Expert City, Colombo (Physical, in-person session)
  • Fee: Rs. 15,000.00 (Includes a copy of the reference book “200 Dos & Don'ts" For Management Research Students)

THEORY TO TRADE BY TRACE

Privacy Policy

Policy Document

Last Updated: June 9, 2026. Learn how Theory to Trade (T2T) by TRACE manages, stores, and protects your personal information.

Sections

  • 1. Introduction
  • 2. Information We Collect
  • 3. How We Use Information
  • 4. Information Sharing
  • 5. Data Security
  • 6. Your Rights
  • 7. Contact Us

01 Introduction

Welcome to Theory to Trade (T2T) by TRACE. We respect your privacy and are committed to protecting the personal data you share with us. This Privacy Policy details how we collect, process, utilize, and protect your information when you enroll in our programs (CRISP, IFAP, Lead-x, etc.), visit our website, or interact with our learning management systems.

By using our services, registering as a student, or supporting as an industrial mentor, you agree to the practices outlined in this policy.

02 Information We Collect

We collect personal information to provide you with the best possible educational and professional matchmaking experiences. The information we collect falls into the following categories:

  • Registration Details: When you register as a student or mentor, we collect personal identifiers such as your full name, email address, contact phone number, university or professional affiliation, and academic details.
  • Professional Dossier & CV: If you apply for programs or internship matchmaking, you may share your Curriculum Vitae (CV), academic transcripts, portfolio links, GitHub username, and LinkedIn profile.
  • Usage Data: When visiting our website, we may collect technical details such as your IP address, browser type, operating system, pages visited, and duration of stay.

03 How We Use Information

We use your personal information strictly for educational, administrative, and professional development purposes, specifically to:

  • Evaluate applications and process enrollment for training cohorts (such as CRISP Practitioner or Lead-x).
  • Provide guided project structures, assign students to team spaces, and pair student groups with appropriate mentors.
  • Coordinate and facilitate live physical workshops and virtual mentoring sessions.
  • Reach out to you with important updates, program announcements, newsletters, and registration materials.
  • Benchmark program progress and monitor training cohort metrics.

04 Information Sharing

TRACE does not sell, lease, or distribute your personal data to third-party advertising or marketing services. However, in order to bridge the gap between academic theory and trade, we share candidate profiles under strict guidelines:

  • With Mentors: Academic credentials, CVs, and project submissions are shared with certified TRACE mentors to facilitate code reviews and professional guidance.
  • With Corporate Partners: CVs and project portfolios of students enrolled in Practitioner tracks are shared with our partner network (e.g. Nagarro, 99x, ThinkTank, Worklenz, etc.) to evaluate candidates for internships or employment positions.
  • Legal Compliance: We may disclose information if required by Sri Lankan law or regulatory authorities.

T2T Guide chat: When AI assistance is used, your question, recent conversation, and relevant public website passages are sent to OpenRouter and its selected model provider to generate a reply. Recent messages are stored in this browser tab’s session storage; use Start a new chat to clear them. Please do not send passwords, payment details, or sensitive personal information. Learn more in OpenRouter’s privacy policy.

05 Data Security

The security of your personal data is critical to us. We employ standard technical and administrative safeguards to protect your personal information against unauthorized access, theft, alteration, or loss. This includes secure hosting servers, access control boundaries, and encrypted communication channels.

Please remember that no method of transmission over the Internet or method of electronic storage is 100% secure, and we cannot guarantee its absolute safety.

06 Your Rights

You have control over how your data is managed. Depending on your program enrollment state, you hold the following rights:

  • Right of Access: You can request a summary of the personal information we currently hold for you.
  • Right to Correct: You can ask us to update or modify outdated or incorrect information in our system at any time.
  • Right to Erasure: You can request that we delete your application records or registration data. Please note that requesting deletion may affect your ability to participate in ongoing programs or receive program credentials.

07 Contact Us

If you have any questions, concerns, or requests regarding this Privacy Policy or your data management, please contact the TRACE team.
